newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's Velayati says Gulf Arab tour successful.
newsitem.headline: Iran's Velayati says Gulf Arab tour successful.

text.p: Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said his tour of six Gulf Arab this week opened a new chapter in ties with its oil-rich neighbours.

"The visit has been highly successful in view of the wide-scale negative propaganda launched by the Americans against Iran," Velayati told the official Iranian news agency IRNA before leaving the United Arab Emirates (UAE) late on Thursday.
Iran's relations with its Gulf Arab neighbours are often tense. Gulf Arab states have accused Iran of interfering in their internal affairs, a charge which Iran denies.
Velayati said top officials he met in Saudi Arabia, Oman, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and the UAE "noted the significance of relations with Tehran".
"And despite the poisonous (U.S.) propaganda, they were willing to expand their relations with Tehran," he added.
Velayati carried letters from President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani inviting heads of the Gulf Arab states to a summit of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference in Tehran in December.
He told IRNA his talks with King Fahd of Saudi Arabia, Crown Prince Abdullah and Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal could "serve as a turning point in Tehran-Riyadh relations".
Riyadh has refused to confirm U.S. media reports of an Iranian link to a bomb attack that killed 19 U.S. servicemen in the eastern Saudi city of Khobar last June.
Iran -- which Washington has accused of sponsoring state terrorism and has imposed sanctions on -- denies any role.
